part.plateau.reference.title: Leveled plateau reference
part.plateau.reference.simple: A simple engineering reference plane used to locate the pyramid and passages in one coordinate frame.
part.plateau.reference.why_known: It is a derived modeling datum, not a claim that the modern plateau is perfectly flat.

part.pyramid.khafre.title: Khafre pyramid envelope
part.pyramid.khafre.simple: The reconstructed original geometric envelope of Khafre’s pyramid — the clean outer form before later erosion and casing loss.
part.pyramid.khafre.why_known: Its dimensions come from historical survey measurements and surviving architectural evidence, not from the controversial deep-structure claims.
questions: Does the exact 53°10′ slope create unusual physical behavior?
How much do predicted effects change if the slope or height is perturbed?

part.casing.granite.lower.title: Lower granite casing belt
part.casing.granite.lower.simple: A separately modeled lower casing zone so material and geometry can be inspected independently.
part.casing.granite.lower.why_known: Historical descriptions and surviving casing distinguish this zone from the limestone core.

part.upper.entrance.existing.title: Measured / derived passage segment
part.upper.entrance.existing.simple: A real passage segment reconstructed as its own spatial object. Select it to see its dimensions, coordinates, connections and evidence.
part.upper.entrance.existing.why_known: These segments are constrained by published survey geometry. Missing original extensions are modeled separately rather than silently merged.

part.upper.entrance.reconstructed.title: Upper entrance — reconstructed extension
part.upper.entrance.reconstructed.simple: A reconstructed continuation through lost casing needed to visualize the original entrance path.
part.upper.entrance.reconstructed.why_known: This extension is derived from the surviving passage geometry; it is not treated as directly surviving fabric.

part.lower.entrance.reconstructed.title: Lower entrance — reconstructed extension
part.lower.entrance.reconstructed.simple: A reconstructed continuation through the original pavement/terrace zone.
part.lower.entrance.reconstructed.why_known: It is retained as DERIVED geometry so the original path can be visualized without calling it directly measured.

part.upper.roll.title: Upper half-round roof roll
part.upper.roll.simple: A distinct shaped element in the upper entrance system.
part.upper.roll.why_known: It is preserved as a separate entity because its geometry differs from the rectangular passage around it.

part.upper.portcullis.slab.title: Upper granite portcullis slab
part.upper.portcullis.slab.simple: A granite blocking element associated with the upper entrance route.
part.upper.portcullis.slab.why_known: It is modeled separately from the corridor because material, dimensions and function are distinct.

part.lower.turning_recess.title: Lower-route turning recess
part.lower.turning_recess.simple: A local widening/recess in the lower passage system.
part.lower.turning_recess.why_known: Its location is derived from the surveyed passage network.

part.lower.chamber.title: Lower / subsidiary chamber
part.lower.chamber.simple: A known rock-cut chamber on the lower route — part of Khafre’s actual internal architecture, not the viral deep-shaft claim.
part.lower.chamber.why_known: Its plan and location are reconstructed from published measurements.

part.lower.portcullis.slab.title: Lower portcullis — unresolved envelope
part.lower.portcullis.slab.simple: A placeholder envelope for a lower blocking element whose exact geometry has not yet been resolved to the same standard as the main survey network.
part.lower.portcullis.slab.why_known: ATLAS deliberately keeps this ASSUMED so later evidence can replace it cleanly.
questions: Resolve exact slab dimensions and placement from stronger source material.

part.burial.chamber.title: Main burial chamber
part.burial.chamber.simple: The principal chamber containing Khafre’s granite sarcophagus. The walls, gabled roof envelope and fine floor layer are separate inspectable objects.
part.burial.chamber.why_known: The chamber survives, has been surveyed and photographed, and is part of the established internal plan.
questions: Compare measured chamber geometry with acoustic and structural modes without assuming intentional resonance.

part.sarcophagus.body.title: Khafre granite sarcophagus
part.sarcophagus.body.simple: The granite coffer inside the burial chamber. Body and lid are separate objects so their geometry can be inspected and exploded.
part.sarcophagus.body.why_known: The object survives in place and is documented by both measurements and photographs.

part.upper.1.title: Reported Upper Structure 1
part.upper.1.simple: This object is part of the controversial deep-structure reconstruction. It is included so the claim can be tested geometrically — not because ATLAS considers it discovered.
part.upper.1.why_known: No independently verified photograph or direct subsurface measurement confirms this exact object. It remains isolated in the UNVERIFIED layer.
questions: Can seismic, gravity, resistivity or another independent method recover this same geometry?
Would a void of this size produce a detectable physical signature?
Are repeated shapes more consistent with engineered construction or reconstruction artifacts?
